atoms.text: This level includes mentions of uncomfortable situations both at school and at home. If this level upsets you, you should speak with a trusted adult about it.

instruction.text: Read the scenario where someone’s behaviour has made someone else uncomfortable. Find all the examples of this in the text.

atoms.b: Amelia tripped over on stage during a school play and is now very embarrassed. She doesn’t want to talk about it, ((but_her_friends_keep_bringing_it_up)). ((They_also_tell_their_other_friends_all_about_it,_because_they_think_it’s_okay_to_joke_about_it.))
atoms.sound: Amelia tripped over on stage during a school play and is now very embarrassed. She doesn’t want to talk about it, but her friends keep bringing it up. They also tell their other friends all about it, because they think it’s okay to joke about it.

instruction.text: Why is this behaviour not okay? Select all the correct answers.

b: ++They are disrespecting Amelia’s privacy.
++They are crossing Amelia’s boundaries.
They are pushing unwanted physical contact onto Amelia.

instruction.text: What should Amelia do about this? Select all the correct answers.

feedback.end: Your friends might not mean harm, but their behaviour can still upset you. If they are doing things that make you upset, you should let them know that it is not okay.

b: ++Tell them to stop because it makes her upset.
++Tell a teacher about it if they won’t leave her alone.
Get revenge by spilling their secrets to other people.

instruction.text: Read the scenario where someone’s behaviour has made someone else uncomfortable. Find all the examples of this in the text.

atoms.b: ((Ethan’s_friend_Callum_is_very_rough_when_playing_and_likes_to_push_him_around)). ((Ethan_has_told_him_to_stop_because_it_hurts_him,_but_Callum_refuses.)) He wants to tell a teacher about this, but he’s afraid that it will affect their friendship.
atoms.sound: Ethan’s friend Callum is very rough when playing and likes to push him around. Ethan has told him to stop because it hurts him, but Callum refuses. He wants to tell a teacher about this, but he’s afraid that it will affect their friendship.

instruction.text: Why is this behaviour not okay? Select all the correct answers.

b: ++Callum is crossing Ethan’s boundaries.
++Callum is pushing unwanted physical contact onto Ethan.
Callum is disrespecting Ethan’s privacy.

instruction.text: What should Ethan do about this? Select all the correct answers.

feedback.end: Some children enjoy playing rough and are not aware that this might hurt you. If they don’t stop even when you tell them to, you should tell an adult.

b: ++Rethink whether Callum is really a good friend and distance himself from him.
++Tell a teacher about it even if it’ll affect the friendship.
Push Callum back harder to prove that he is stronger than him.

instruction.text: Read the scenario where someone’s behaviour has made someone else uncomfortable. Find all the examples of this in the text.

atoms.b: Krish did badly in his maths test and doesn’t want anyone to know. ((His_classmates_keep_trying_to_ask_him_about_it,_which_makes_him_nervous)). While walking home from school, ((his_classmates_tackle_him_and_hold_him_down,_so_that_they_can_find_his_test_paper_in_his_bag.
atoms.sound: Krish did badly in his maths test and doesn’t want anyone to know. His classmates keep trying to ask him about it, which makes him nervous. While walking home from school, his classmates tackle him and hold him down, so that they can find his test paper in his bag.

instruction.text: Why is this behaviour not okay? Select all the correct answers.

b: ++They are disrespecting Krish’s privacy.
++They are crossing Krish’s boundaries.
++They are pushing unwanted physical contact onto Krish.

instruction.text: What should Krish do about this? Select all the correct answers.

feedback.end: This behaviour from Krish’s classmates counts as bullying. Other children at school should never be allowed to deliberately hurt or upset you. You should always tell a trusted adult, so they can stop this behaviour.

b: ++Shout out for help from anyone nearby.
++Tell his parents about it when he gets back home.
Never go back to school again.

instruction.text: Read the scenario where someone’s behaviour has made someone else uncomfortable. Find all the examples of this in the text.

atoms.b: Katie’s uncle comes over to take care of her when her parents go away on business trips. He buys lots of gifts for her, but ((she_feels_uncomfortable_around_him_because_he_keeps_trying_to_touch_her)). She has also noticed that ((he_has_been_in_her_room_and_looked_through_her_private_diary)).
atoms.sound: Katie’s uncle comes over to take care of her when her parents go away on business trips. He buys lots of gifts for her, but she feels uncomfortable around him because he keeps trying to touch her. She has also noticed that he has been in her room and looked through her private diary.

instruction.text: Why is this behaviour not okay? Select all the correct answers.

b: ++Katie’s uncle is disrespecting her privacy.
++Katie’s uncle is crossing her boundaries.
++Katie’s uncle is pushing unwanted physical contact onto her.

instruction.text: What should Katie do about this? Select all the correct answers.

feedback.end: Katie’s uncle’s behaviour is abusive. Even though he is a family member, he should never be allowed to inappropriately touch Katie or enter her room without her permission. Any adult treating you like this, whether it’s a stranger or someone you know, must always be reported immediately.

b: ++Tell her parents about this immediately and make sure they will not let this continue.
++Call Childline or the police.
Stay quiet about it because he is family.
